Scenarios as documentation

Source: R/features_rd.R
features_rd.Rd

Put scenarios of your feature files in the help page of a function, so that readers of the help find how it behaves. Call it with @eval in the function's roxygen block:

#' Add items to a basket
#' @eval cucumber::features_rd(features = "basket.feature")
#' @export
add <- function(basket, n) basket + n

It adds a section, named "Behavior" by default, with each selected feature: its name, its description, the Rules and Backgrounds of the selected scenarios and the scenarios, without their tags. Of a Scenario Outline, only the selected Examples rows are shown.

In the help page, each feature is one block of Gherkin, as it's written. On HTML pages, like the pkgdown reference page, it's shown like Markdown with Gherkin: the names of the feature and of its Rules, Backgrounds, scenarios and Examples are headers, steps are a list, tables are tables and Doc Strings are code, a Doc String of Gherkin highlighted as Gherkin. With markdown = FALSE, HTML pages show the block of Gherkin too.

Scenarios are selected like in test(). By default only scenarios matching "@rd" are selected, so that you choose the ones that make good documentation. Set the cucumber.rd_tags option to use another tag expression, or pass tags = NULL to select scenarios without a tag.

On a pkgdown site, code is highlighted by the site's theme.

It turns on markdown for the roxygen block it's in.

Usage

features_rd(
  path = getOption("cucumber.path"),
  filter = NULL,
  tags = getOption("cucumber.rd_tags"),
  name = NULL,
  features = NULL,
  section = getOption("cucumber.rd_section"),
  markdown = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

path

Path to the directory containing the .feature files. Its subdirectories are searched too. Defaults to the cucumber.path option, see opts. Relative paths are relative to the working directory, the package's root when you run devtools::document().

filter

If not NULL, only features with file names matching this regular expression are documented. Matching is performed on the file name after it's stripped of ".feature" or ".feature.md".

tags

If not NULL, select scenarios by tag expression string, see test(). Defaults to the cucumber.rd_tags option, see opts.

name

If not NULL, only scenarios with names matching any of these regular expressions are documented.

features

If not NULL, only these feature files are documented. Relative paths are relative to path. A directory selects the feature files in it and its subdirectories. Add :line to select only the scenario at that line, e.g. "addition.feature:12". The line of an example row selects only that example.

section

Name of the section. Defaults to the cucumber.rd_section option, see opts.

markdown

If TRUE, HTML pages show each feature like Markdown with Gherkin. If FALSE, they show it as one block of Gherkin, as it's written, like the help page.

...

Additional arguments passed to grepl().

Value

Lines of roxygen tags, for @eval.

Behavior






Feature: Scenarios as documentation


features_rd() puts scenarios of feature files in the help page of a function, in a
"Behavior" section, so readers of the help find how it behaves. Call it with @eval
in the function's roxygen block. It selects scenarios like test(): by features and their
lines, filter, name and tags. By default only scenarios tagged @rd are selected,
set the cucumber.rd_tags option to use another tag expression. Name the section with
section, or for every help page with the cucumber.rd_section option.


In the help page, each feature is one block of Gherkin, as it's written. On HTML pages, like
the pkgdown reference page, it's shown like Markdown with Gherkin: its name and the names of
its Rules, Backgrounds, scenarios and Examples are headers, its steps a list, its tables tables
and its Doc Strings code, a Doc String of Gherkin highlighted. With markdown = FALSE, HTML
pages show the block of Gherkin too.


Background:
  • Given a package
    • 

  • And a file named "tests/acceptance/basket.feature" with

    Feature: Basket
  A basket holds the items a customer wants to buy.

  Background:
    Given an empty basket

  @rd
  Scenario: Add an item
    When I add 1 item
    Then the basket has 1 item

  @example
  Scenario: Remove an item from an empty basket
    When I remove 1 item
    Then the basket is empty

  @rd
  Scenario Outline: Add items
    When I add <n> items
    Then the basket has <n> items

    Examples:
      | n |
      | 2 |
      | 3 |
    •

#' @export

    Then the basket has <n> items    Examples:

      | 2 |
